paragraphs: Rav Chiyya bar Yosef: Ketubot 111b, several statements. In the time of Rav, Shmuel, and R. Yochanan. Rabbah, portion Naso, section 9, and Jerusalem Sotah, chapter 1, halakhah 3: he sent three students after his wife. Mattenot Kehunah suggests that she had been taken captive, like the story of Zekharyah ben HaKatzav. He instituted a regulation at Sikhra: end of HaUmanin. “R. Chiyya bar Yosef said: they taught this only, etc.; R. Yochanan said, etc.; Rav Pappa said: they do not disagree”—Chullin 90a. Thus R. Chiyya bar Yosef is put before R. Yochanan. Bekhorot 39a has R. Chiyya bar Yosi. And R. Abbahu. “R. Oshaya said”—Avodah Zarah 51b; Sanhedrin 16b. Rav Acha bar Yosef—perhaps his brother. R. Ilai, in his name. Bereshit Rabbah, end of section 55: R. Chiyya bar Yokhi—perhaps it should read Yosi—in R. Meyasha's name, and he taught it in R. Benayah's name. R. Levi told him, “Enough for you.” Rav Giddel, in his name: Avodah Zarah 50a; Shabbat, chapter 1, 7a. Pesachim 7a: “R. Giddel said: R. Chiyya bar Yosi said: Rav said.” There, 21b, that matter is in R. Yochanan's name. “R. Giddel said: R. Chiyya bar Yosef said: Rav concedes”—Eruvin 90b. Rav Giddel bar Binyamin said: R. Chiyya bar Yosef, in Rav's name. Rav Dimi—perhaps his brother. R. Chiyya bar Abba spoke in his name: Kilayim, chapter 4. R. Chanina—perhaps his brother. R. Chama—perhaps his brother; it is likely that they are one person and there is a scribal error; see there. When he came up, he stated Rav's teachings before R. Yochanan: Gittin 39a; Chullin 54a. He taught before R. Yochanan: Kirah, 45a; Beitzah 30b. He asked before R. Yochanan: Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of chapter 6 of Nazir. They gave him money for salt; eventually salt became dearer, and he came before R. Yochanan: Bava Metzia 48b. Rav Yitzchak—perhaps his brother. R. Levi; see above. R. Meyasha; see above. He leaned on Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak's shoulder; see Rav Acha bar Yosef above. Before Rav Nachman: Beitzah 32b. In Rav's name; see above. He stated Rav's teaching before Shmuel: Shabbat 53a. He asked Shmuel: Yevamot 58b, near the end. He said to Shmuel, “Does the law follow you or Rav?” He answered, “Rav”: Eruvin 90b. He replied to Resh Lakish: Temurah 7a.
